body:
MediaDive recipe lookup currently removes punctuation before resolving ingredient identity (`get_compounds_of_solution`). Its translation table removes parentheses, so the existing independently supported mapping for `Ca(NO3)2 x 4 H2O` is queried as `CaNO32 x 4 H2O` and lost. The actual compound resolver retains CHEBI:86159 (native calcium nitrate tetrahydrate); 41 recipe routes become source-local after unsafe anhydrous fallback is correctly rejected.

The same method uses display normalization for nested-solution identity and mutates cached compound recipe records in place. A second lookup therefore no longer has the original source spelling available.

Observed on frozen integration a0089a37c5e390ad013ded7e8c54dd52cbf31868 and reviewed unified candidate SHA256 9e481e31f23b7a2414537f967ea513a7b494824799a002ca4300765f5acea0f1. Evidence: data/mim-ship-20260925.QDVfoK/all-media-{before,after}-hydrates.json and all-media-hydrate-delta.json. Native CHEBI:86159 includes synonym `Ca(NO3)2.4H2O`.

Fix scope: preserve original source names for compound and nested-solution lookup/admission; retain display cleanup separately; avoid mutating cached source records. Do not introduce fuzzy formula equivalence, guessed hydrate identities, or source-specific target exceptions. Add hermetic routing, safety, and repeat-call tests; rerun complete MediaDive route inventory and quantify any other changes.
title: Preserve source chemical scope before MediaDive recipe display normalization
